You now have the building blocks of AI readiness: a framework to assess where you stand, tools to find and prioritize use cases, methods to audit and fix data, approaches for people and change, and the governance, metrics and pilot discipline needed to scale. The final step is to turn them into a practical plan.

A 90-day structure

PeriodFocusKey outputs
Days 1–30Assess and alignReadiness assessment with evidence, sponsor named, acceptable-use policy issued, use-case discovery workshop held
Days 31–60Prioritize and prepareScored value–effort matrix, one quick win chosen, data audit completed, business case and pilot charter approved
Days 61–90Pilot and learnPilot running with baseline and weekly PDCA, skills plan under way, data fixes in progress for the next strategic bet

Plan for the weakest dimensions

Return to your readiness assessment. For each dimension scoring 1 or 2, write one action that will lift it by one level within 90 days. Keep actions small and specific, such as "name data owners for sales and inventory data" rather than "improve data governance".

A worked example

Imagine a 55-person industrial distributor. Its assessment scores governance at 1, data quality at 2 and use-case pipeline at 2, with stronger culture and infrastructure. Its 90-day plan:

  • Week 2: issue a two-page AI acceptable-use policy and an AI register.
  • Week 4: run a discovery workshop on order-to-cash; build the pipeline.
  • Week 6: score eight ideas; choose order extraction as the quick win and demand forecasting as the strategic bet.
  • Week 8: complete a data audit on sales history; begin logging stock-outs.
  • Week 9: approve the business case and pilot charter for order extraction.
  • Weeks 10–13: run the pilot with weekly reviews; reassess readiness at day 90.

Keep the cycle going

  1. Reassess readiness every six months and compare the radar chart shape.
  2. Refresh the use-case pipeline quarterly.
  3. Review the AI register and policies at least twice a year.
  4. Share results openly, including stopped pilots and lessons learned.
Readiness is not a gate you pass once. It is a capability you build with every use case.

Complete the final exam to earn your Chmltech certificate of completion. Then put the first two weeks of your plan on the calendar today, while the ideas are fresh.
takeaways: Structure the next 90 days as assess and align, prioritize and prepare, then pilot and learn.
Target one specific action for each readiness dimension scoring 1 or 2.
Reassess readiness, refresh the pipeline and review governance regularly to build lasting capability.
steps.apply: Write your own 90-day AI readiness plan using the three-period structure. Include at least one action for each low-scoring dimension, name an owner for each action and book the first two actions in your calendar.

check.q: In the 90-day plan structure, which output belongs in the first 30 days?
opts: Pilot running with weekly PDCA reviews
Readiness assessment completed and sponsor named
check.why: The first period focuses on assessing and aligning, which includes the readiness assessment and naming a sponsor.

labs.title: AI Readiness Self-Assessment
labs.intro: Score your organization from 1 to 5 on seven readiness dimensions to see your maturity profile on a radar chart. Use the result to find the weakest dimension that will set the pace of your AI journey.

dimensions.name: Strategy and leadership
dimensions.question: How clearly have leaders linked AI to business goals, named sponsors and committed resources?
dimensions.low: Name an executive sponsor and write problem statements for your top two business goals before choosing any tool.
dimensions.high: Review your AI priorities against the business plan each year and make sponsors accountable for measured outcomes.

dimensions.name: Use-case pipeline
dimensions.question: How well do you identify, document and prioritize candidate AI use cases?
dimensions.low: Run a process discovery workshop on one core process and start a shared use-case register.
dimensions.high: Refresh the pipeline quarterly and re-score ideas as your data and skills improve.

dimensions.name: Data quality
dimensions.question: How accurate, complete and consistent is the data your key processes depend on?
dimensions.low: Audit the two or three tables your priority use case needs and fix the root causes of the worst gap.
dimensions.high: Keep a monthly data quality scorecard and extend it to the data needed by your next use cases.

dimensions.name: Data infrastructure
dimensions.question: How easily can data be accessed, combined and moved securely between your systems?
dimensions.low: Map the systems your priority use case needs and set up scheduled exports to replace manual data gathering.
dimensions.high: Formalize data pipelines, access controls and monitoring so several AI use cases can share the same foundation.

dimensions.name: Skills and capabilities
dimensions.question: How well do leaders, users and technical staff understand and work with AI tools?
dimensions.low: Build an AI skills matrix for key roles and run basic safe-use training for everyone.
dimensions.high: Develop internal champions who coach others and document reusable prompts, templates and lessons.

dimensions.name: Culture and change
dimensions.question: How open is your organization to experimenting with new tools and adopting new ways of working?
dimensions.low: Involve respected frontline staff in your first pilot and communicate openly about how freed time will be used.
dimensions.high: Share results, including stopped pilots, and recognize teams that improve processes with AI.

dimensions.name: Governance and risk
dimensions.question: How well defined are your rules for AI acceptable use, privacy, risk review and accountability?
dimensions.low: Issue a short acceptable-use policy and start an AI register listing every tool, its owner and impact tier.
dimensions.high: Review the AI register and policies twice a year and tier new use cases by impact before approval.

labs.title: AI Use-Case Prioritization Matrix
labs.intro: Rate each AI use case on effort or feasibility difficulty and on business value to see which are quick wins and which are strategic bets. Rename or add items to reflect your own pipeline.

items.name: Staff assistant for procedures and SOPs

labs.title: AI Use-Case ROI Calculator
labs.intro: Enter the manual hours, labour cost, share of work automatable and the build and running costs of an AI use case to estimate annual savings, payback and three-year ROI. Use it to test the assumptions in your business case.

config.note: Run conservative and optimistic scenarios, and only count saved hours that will genuinely be redeployed or avoid real cost.

exam.q: A 50-person manufacturer has enthusiastic staff and good IT systems but no agreed reason for using AI and no sponsor. What should it do first?
opts: Name a sponsor and define the business problems AI should address
Buy the most popular AI platform
exam.why: Strategic readiness, a sponsor and clear problems, is the missing foundation; tools and hires come after.

exam.q: Which task is best suited to AI rather than simple rule-based automation?
opts: Copying a fixed field from one system to another every night
Sending a reminder email on a set date
Interpreting free-text customer complaints and routing them by topic
Calculating sales tax with a fixed rate
exam.why: Free-text complaints vary widely, which suits AI; the other tasks follow fixed rules.

exam.q: A forecasting pilot worked well on a hand-cleaned dataset but performed poorly on live data. Which pilot-design flaw does this illustrate?
opts: Pilot data did not represent production data
exam.why: Hand-cleaned samples hide the messiness of live data, so results do not carry over to production.

exam.q: A team wants AI to speed up a process with three redundant approval steps. What does Lean thinking recommend?
opts: Automate all three steps with AI
Add a fourth approval for AI output
Remove the redundant steps before considering AI
exam.why: Automating waste only makes waste faster; simplify the process first.

exam.q: On a readiness assessment, an organization scores 4 on skills and culture but 1 on governance. What is the most sensible priority?
opts: Issue an acceptable-use policy and set up an AI register
exam.why: The weakest dimension sets the pace; capable, keen staff without rules are a governance risk.

exam.q: Which problem statement is most useful for starting an AI initiative?
opts: We need a generative AI strategy.
Estimators spend two days per quote, and slow quotes are losing bids to faster competitors.
IT wants to try a new platform.
exam.why: It describes a measurable operational problem and its business impact without assuming a solution.

exam.q: During use-case scoring, an idea is rated value 2 and effort 5. Which quadrant is it in and what is the usual action?
opts: Avoid or rethink; park or reframe the problem
exam.why: Low value with high effort belongs in avoid or rethink.

exam.q: An engineering office wants AI drafting help and already licenses an office suite that includes a generative AI assistant. What is the most sensible route?
opts: Evaluate the existing feature first and invest in approved content and review rules
exam.why: Using features already owned is usually fastest and cheapest for common needs.

exam.q: A business case shows a payback period that is only acceptable under the optimistic scenario. What does this suggest?
opts: The project is a risky bet whose assumptions need testing
The conservative scenario should be deleted
exam.why: If value depends on optimistic assumptions, the case is fragile and those assumptions should be tested in a pilot.

exam.q: A data audit finds that only 60% of maintenance work orders have a failure code. Which data quality dimension is this?
exam.why: Missing required values is a completeness problem.

exam.q: To check the accuracy of inventory records, what is the most reliable method?
opts: Count how many records have blank fields
Compare a random sample of records with a physical count
Check that dates are in the right format
exam.why: Accuracy means data matches reality, which is tested by comparing records to the physical world.

exam.q: An SME's systems offer scheduled exports and some integrations, but there is no central reporting database. Which infrastructure level fits best?
exam.why: Systems that can export data and have some integrations, without a central store, are at the connected level.

exam.q: A clinic plans to use an AI vendor to summarize patient intake forms. Which check is most important before going live?
opts: Confirm where data is stored and processed, whether the vendor uses it for training, and who can access summaries
Check that the tool has an attractive interface
Make sure the summaries are long
Confirm the vendor has many customers
exam.why: Personal health information requires privacy and security checks, including vendor data use and access control.

exam.q: A fabrication shop cleaned its job-hours data once, but quality fell again within months. Which approach would prevent recurrence?
opts: Cleaning the data again every quarter
Buying a more advanced AI model
Using DMAIC to fix root causes in how the data is entered and adding control measures
exam.why: Fixing the entry process and controlling it addresses root causes rather than symptoms.

exam.q: A skills matrix shows that inside sales staff will be the main users of AI order entry but rate low on judging output quality. What is the best response?
opts: Hire a data scientist for the sales team
Train them on reviewing AI output and pair them with super users
exam.why: Targeted training and super-user support close the specific gap the use case depends on.

exam.q: In a RACI chart, who should normally be accountable for operational outcomes of an AI-supported process?
exam.why: The process owner lives with the results daily and should own operational outcomes.

exam.q: Inspectors fear an AI vision system will eliminate their jobs. Which approach best supports adoption?
opts: Explain the business problem, be specific about their future role and involve them in training and testing the system
Introduce the system without notice to avoid resistance
exam.why: Honest communication and involvement build awareness, desire and trust, supporting ADKAR outcomes.

exam.q: Which use case should be classified as high impact for AI governance?
opts: Suggesting stock reorder quantities for review
exam.why: Outputs affecting people's employment are high impact and require strong safeguards and human decisions.

exam.q: A distributor measures extraction accuracy, minutes per order and customer-reported errors. What additional type of metric would catch unintended harm such as missed shipping cut-offs?
exam.why: Guardrail metrics protect against harm elsewhere in the process while targets are pursued.

exam.q: Months after scaling, an AI forecast becomes less accurate as the company adds new product lines. Which practice should have detected this early?
opts: Ongoing monitoring with triggers in a control plan
exam.why: Monitoring tool performance with defined triggers is how drift is detected and acted on after go-live.
